definitions.gloss: oden; Japanese stew with various ingredients in broth
definitions.explanation: A winter comfort food consisting of various ingredients simmered in a light dashi-based broth. Common ingredients include boiled eggs, daikon radish, konjac, fish cakes, tofu, and more.

examples.japanese: {寒|さむ}い{日|ひ}はおでんが{食|た}べたくなる。
examples.english: On cold days I crave oden.

examples.japanese: コンビニのおでんは{冬|ふゆ}の{定番|ていばん}だ。
examples.english: Convenience store oden is a winter staple.

examples.japanese: おでんの{具|ぐ}で{一番|いちばん}{好|す}きなのは{大根|だいこん}と{卵|たまご}だ。
examples.english: My favorite oden ingredients are daikon radish and egg.

notes:
A quintessential Japanese winter dish. In Japan, おでん is famously sold at convenience stores (コンビニ) during the cold months, where customers can choose individual pieces from a heated pot at the counter.

COMMON INGREDIENTS:
- {大根|だいこん} (daikon radish)
- {卵|たまご} (boiled egg)
- こんにゃく (konjac)
- ちくわ (tube-shaped fish cake)
- はんぺん (fish cake)
- {厚揚|あつあ}げ (thick fried tofu)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- おでんの{具|ぐ} (oden ingredients)
- おでん{種|だね} (oden ingredients — more traditional term)
- おでんを{煮込|にこ}む (to simmer oden)

Regional variations exist: {関東|かんとう} style uses a darker soy-based broth, while {関西|かんさい} style uses a lighter dashi broth.
